030/**
031 * NetworkTables Instance.
032 *
033 * <p>Instances are completely independent from each other. Table operations on one instance will
034 * not be visible to other instances unless the instances are connected via the network. The main
035 * limitation on instances is that you cannot have two servers on the same network port. The main
036 * utility of instances is for unit testing, but they can also enable one program to connect to two
037 * different NetworkTables networks.
038 *
039 * <p>The global "default" instance (as returned by {@link #getDefault()}) is always available, and
040 * is intended for the common case when there is only a single NetworkTables instance being used in
041 * the program.
042 *
043 * <p>Additional instances can be created with the {@link #create()} function. A reference must be
044 * kept to the NetworkTableInstance returned by this function to keep it from being garbage
045 * collected.
046 */
047public final class NetworkTableInstance implements AutoCloseable {

052

055

068    /**

587  private Topic[] topicHandlesToTopics(int[] handles) {
588    Topic[] topics = new Topic[handles.length];
589    for (int i = 0; i < handles.length; i++) {
590      topics[i] = getCachedTopic(handles[i]);
591    }
592    return topics;
593  }

741  /* Cache of created tables. */
742  private final ConcurrentMap<String, NetworkTable> m_tables = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
743
744  /**
745   * Gets the table with the specified key.
746   *
747   * @param key the key name
748   * @return The network table
749   */
750  public NetworkTable getTable(String key) {
751    // prepend leading / if not present
752    String theKey;
753    if (key.isEmpty() || "/".equals(key)) {
754      theKey = "";
755    } else if (key.charAt(0) == NetworkTable.PATH_SEPARATOR) {
756      theKey = key;
757    } else {
758      theKey = NetworkTable.PATH_SEPARATOR + key;
759    }
760
761    // cache created tables
762    NetworkTable table = m_tables.get(theKey);
763    if (table == null) {
764      table = new NetworkTable(this, theKey);
765      NetworkTable oldTable = m_tables.putIfAbsent(theKey, table);
766      if (oldTable != null) {
767        table = oldTable;
768      }
769    }
770    return table;
771  }

777  private static class ListenerStorage implements AutoCloseable {
778    private final ReentrantLock m_lock = new ReentrantLock();
779    private final Map<Integer, Consumer<NetworkTableEvent>> m_listeners = new HashMap<>();
780
781    @SuppressWarnings("PMD.SingularField")
782    private Thread m_thread;
783
784    private int m_poller;
785    private boolean m_waitQueue;
786    private final Event m_waitQueueEvent = new Event();
787    private final Condition m_waitQueueCond = m_lock.newCondition();
788    private final NetworkTableInstance m_inst;
789
790    ListenerStorage(NetworkTableInstance inst) {
791      m_inst = inst;
792    }
793
794    int add(
795        String[] prefixes,
796        EnumSet<NetworkTableEvent.Kind> eventKinds,
797        Consumer<NetworkTableEvent> listener) {
798      m_lock.lock();
799      try {
800        if (m_poller == 0) {
801          m_poller = NetworkTablesJNI.createListenerPoller(m_inst.getHandle());
802          startThread();
803        }
804        int h = NetworkTablesJNI.addListener(m_poller, prefixes, eventKinds);
805        m_listeners.put(h, listener);
806        return h;
807      } finally {
808        m_lock.unlock();
809      }
810    }
811
812    int add(
813        int handle,
814        EnumSet<NetworkTableEvent.Kind> eventKinds,
815        Consumer<NetworkTableEvent> listener) {
816      m_lock.lock();
817      try {
818        if (m_poller == 0) {
819          m_poller = NetworkTablesJNI.createListenerPoller(m_inst.getHandle());
820          startThread();
821        }
822        int h = NetworkTablesJNI.addListener(m_poller, handle, eventKinds);
823        m_listeners.put(h, listener);
824        return h;
825      } finally {
826        m_lock.unlock();
827      }
828    }
829
830    int addLogger(int minLevel, int maxLevel, Consumer<NetworkTableEvent> listener) {
831      m_lock.lock();
832      try {
833        if (m_poller == 0) {
834          m_poller = NetworkTablesJNI.createListenerPoller(m_inst.getHandle());
835          startThread();
836        }
837        int h = NetworkTablesJNI.addLogger(m_poller, minLevel, maxLevel);
838        m_listeners.put(h, listener);
839        return h;
840      } finally {
841        m_lock.unlock();
842      }
843    }
844
845    void remove(int listener) {
846      m_lock.lock();
847      try {
848        m_listeners.remove(listener);
849      } finally {
850        m_lock.unlock();
851      }
852      NetworkTablesJNI.removeListener(listener);
853    }
854
855    @Override
856    public void close() {
857      if (m_poller != 0) {
858        NetworkTablesJNI.destroyListenerPoller(m_poller);
859      }
860      m_poller = 0;
861    }
862
863    @SuppressWarnings("PMD.AvoidCatchingGenericException")
864    private void startThread() {
865      m_thread =
866          new Thread(
867              () -> {
868                boolean wasInterrupted = false;
869                int[] handles = new int[] { m_poller, m_waitQueueEvent.getHandle() };
870                while (!Thread.interrupted()) {
871                  try {
872                    WPIUtilJNI.waitForObjects(handles);
873                  } catch (InterruptedException ex) {
874                    m_lock.lock();
875                    try {
876                      if (m_waitQueue) {
877                        m_waitQueue = false;
878                        m_waitQueueCond.signalAll();
879                      }
880                    } finally {
881                      m_lock.unlock();
882                    }
883                    Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
884                    // don't try to destroy poller, as its handle is likely no longer valid
885                    wasInterrupted = true;
886                    break;
887                  }
888                  for (NetworkTableEvent event :
889                      NetworkTablesJNI.readListenerQueue(m_inst, m_poller)) {
890                    Consumer<NetworkTableEvent> listener;
891                    m_lock.lock();
892                    try {
893                      listener = m_listeners.get(event.listener);
894                    } finally {
895                      m_lock.unlock();
896                    }
897                    if (listener != null) {
898                      try {
899                        listener.accept(event);
900                      } catch (Throwable throwable) {
901                        System.err.println(
902                            "Unhandled exception during listener callback: "
903                            + throwable.toString());
904                        throwable.printStackTrace();
905                      }
906                    }
907                  }
908                  m_lock.lock();
909                  try {
910                    if (m_waitQueue) {
911                      m_waitQueue = false;
912                      m_waitQueueCond.signalAll();
913                    }
914                  } finally {
915                    m_lock.unlock();
916                  }
917                }
918                m_lock.lock();
919                try {
920                  if (!wasInterrupted) {
921                    NetworkTablesJNI.destroyListenerPoller(m_poller);
922                  }
923                  m_poller = 0;
924                } finally {
925                  m_lock.unlock();
926                }
927              },
928              "NTListener");
929      m_thread.setDaemon(true);
930      m_thread.start();
931    }
932
933    boolean waitForQueue(double timeout) {
934      m_lock.lock();
935      try {
936        if (m_poller != 0) {
937          m_waitQueue = true;
938          m_waitQueueEvent.set();
939          while (m_waitQueue) {
940            try {
941              if (timeout < 0) {
942                m_waitQueueCond.await();
943              } else {
944                return m_waitQueueCond.await((long) (timeout * 1e9), TimeUnit.NANOSECONDS);
945              }
946            } catch (InterruptedException ex) {
947              Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
948              return true;
949            }
950          }
951        }
952      } finally {
953        m_lock.unlock();
954      }
955      return true;
956    }
957  }

1129  /**
1130   * Get the current network mode.
1131   *
1132   * @return Enum set of NetworkMode.
1133   */
1134  public EnumSet<NetworkMode> getNetworkMode() {
1135    int flags = NetworkTablesJNI.getNetworkMode(m_handle);
1136    EnumSet<NetworkMode> rv = EnumSet.noneOf(NetworkMode.class);
1137    for (NetworkMode mode : NetworkMode.values()) {
1138      if ((flags & mode.getValue()) != 0) {
1139        rv.add(mode);
1140      }
1141    }
1142    return rv;
1143  }

1463   * 10.TE.AM.2 address is only added if the team string parses as an integer in the range 0
1464   * to 25599 inclusive.
1465   *
1466   * @param team team number string

1468   */

1470    NetworkTablesJNI.setServerFixed(m_handle, team, port);
1471  }

1612  /**
1613   * Returns whether there is a data schema already registered with the given name that this
1614   * instance has published. This does NOT perform a check as to whether the schema has already
1615   * been published by another node on the network.
1616   *
1617   * @param name Name (the string passed as the data type for topics using this schema)
1618   * @return True if schema already registered
1619   */
1620  public boolean hasSchema(String name) {
1621    return m_schemas.containsKey("/.schema/" + name);
1622  }
1623
1624  /**
1625   * Registers a data schema. Data schemas provide information for how a certain data type string
1626   * can be decoded. The type string of a data schema indicates the type of the schema itself (e.g.
1627   * "protobuf" for protobuf schemas, "struct" for struct schemas, etc). In NetworkTables, schemas
1628   * are published just like normal topics, with the name being generated from the provided name:
1629   * "/.schema/name". Duplicate calls to this function with the same name are silently ignored.
1630   *
1631   * @param name Name (the string passed as the data type for topics using this schema)
1632   * @param type Type of schema (e.g. "protobuf", "struct", etc)
1633   * @param schema Schema data
1634   */
1635  public void addSchema(String name, String type, byte[] schema) {
1636    m_schemas.computeIfAbsent("/.schema/" + name, k -> {
1637      RawPublisher pub = getRawTopic(k).publishEx(type, "{\"retained\":true}");
1638      pub.setDefault(schema);
1639      return pub;
1640    });
1641  }
1642
1643  /**
1644   * Registers a data schema. Data schemas provide information for how a certain data type string
1645   * can be decoded. The type string of a data schema indicates the type of the schema itself (e.g.
1646   * "protobuf" for protobuf schemas, "struct" for struct schemas, etc). In NetworkTables, schemas
1647   * are published just like normal topics, with the name being generated from the provided name:
1648   * "/.schema/name". Duplicate calls to this function with the same name are silently ignored.
1649   *
1650   * @param name Name (the string passed as the data type for topics using this schema)
1651   * @param type Type of schema (e.g. "protobuf", "struct", etc)
1652   * @param schema Schema data
1653   */
1654  public void addSchema(String name, String type, String schema) {
1655    m_schemas.computeIfAbsent("/.schema/" + name, k -> {
1656      RawPublisher pub = getRawTopic(k).publishEx(type, "{\"retained\":true}");
1657      pub.setDefault(StandardCharsets.UTF_8.encode(schema));
1658      return pub;
1659    });
1660  }
1661
1662  /**
1663   * Registers a protobuf schema. Duplicate calls to this function with the same name are silently
1664   * ignored.
1665   *
1666   * @param proto protobuf serialization object
1667   */
1668  public void addSchema(Protobuf<?, ?> proto) {
1669    proto.forEachDescriptor(
1670        this::hasSchema,
1671        (typeString, schema) -> addSchema(typeString, "proto:FileDescriptorProto", schema));
1672  }
1673
1674  /**
1675   * Registers a struct schema. Duplicate calls to this function with the same name are silently
1676   * ignored.
1677   *
1678   * @param struct struct serialization object
1679   */
1680  public void addSchema(Struct<?> struct) {
1681    addSchemaImpl(struct, new HashSet<>());
1682  }
1683
1684  @Override
1685  public boolean equals(Object other) {
1686    return other == this || other instanceof NetworkTableInstance inst && m_handle == inst.m_handle;
1687  }
1688
1689  @Override
1690  public int hashCode() {
1691    return m_handle;
1692  }
1693
1694  private void addSchemaImpl(Struct<?> struct, Set<String> seen) {
1695    String typeString = struct.getTypeString();
1696    if (hasSchema(typeString)) {
1697      return;
1698    }
1699    if (!seen.add(typeString)) {
1700      throw new UnsupportedOperationException(typeString + ": circular reference with " + seen);
1701    }
1702    addSchema(typeString, "structschema", struct.getSchema());
1703    for (Struct<?> inner : struct.getNested()) {
1704      addSchemaImpl(inner, seen);
1705    }
1706    seen.remove(typeString);
1707  }
1708
1709  private boolean m_owned;
1710  private int m_handle;
1711  private final ConcurrentMap<String, RawPublisher> m_schemas = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
1712}
